questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The order of $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactivity of the following alkyl bromides toward $\text{NaI}$ in dry acetone is
questions.explanationEn: The Finkelstein reaction ($\text{NaI}$ in dry acetone) proceeds by a concerted backside $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism, whose rate is governed inversely by steric hindrance at the $\alpha$-carbon: methyl $>$ primary $>$ secondary $\gg$ tertiary. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Reaction of cyclohexanone with methylenetriphenylphosphorane ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$) affords
questions.explanationEn: The **Wittig reaction** between a ketone (cyclohexanone) and a phosphorus ylide ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$) replaces the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ oxygen directly with $=\text{CH}_2$ via an oxaphosphetane intermediate, yielding **methylenecyclohexane** and $\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{O}$. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The reagent that reduces an internal alkyne ($\text{R}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{R}$) stereoselectively to the $(E)$-alkene is
questions.explanationEn: Dissolving-metal reduction with $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ proceeds via a vinyl radical anion that equilibrates to the sterically less hindered *trans* geometry prior to protonation, selectively yielding the **$(E)$-alkene**. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Claisen condensation of ethyl acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{Et}$) using $\text{NaOEt}$ in ethanol, a full stoichiometric equivalent of $\text{NaOEt}$ is required rather than a catalytic amount because
optionsEn: $\text{NaOEt}$ is consumed in saponifying the ester
deprotonation of the acidic $\alpha$-methylene proton of the $\beta$-keto ester product drives the unfavorable equilibrium to completion
the tetrahedral intermediate requires two equivalents of alkoxide to collapse
questions.explanationEn: The initial carbon–carbon bond-forming steps in the Claisen condensation are thermodynamically uphill. The irreversible acid–base reaction between $\text{EtO}^-$ and the acidic $\alpha$-methylene group of ethyl acetoacetate ($\text{p}K_a \approx 11$) to form a resonance-stabilized enolate drives the entire reaction to completion, requiring a full equivalent of base (followed by acidic workup). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the free-radical monobromination of 2-methylpropane (isobutane) with $\text{Br}_2/h\nu$, the major product is 2-bromo-2-methylpropane primarily because
optionsEn: the bromine radical is highly unselective and reacts statistically
the hydrogen abstraction step is endothermic with a late, product-like transition state
the hydrogen abstraction step is strongly exothermic with an early transition state
bromination proceeds via a carbocation rearrangement
questions.explanationEn: In free-radical bromination, hydrogen abstraction by $\text{Br}^\bullet$ is endothermic. By the Hammond postulate, the transition state is **late (product-like)**, developing substantial radical character on carbon. Consequently, formation of the more stable tertiary radical is overwhelmingly favored over the primary radical. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Irradiation ($h\nu$) of 2-diazocyclohexan-1-one in methanol gives as the major product
questions.explanationEn: Photolysis of the cyclic $\alpha$-diazoketone 2-diazocyclohexan-1-one triggers the **Wolff rearrangement**: loss of $\text{N}_2$ with ring contraction forms cyclopentylideneketene (cyclopentylketene), which is trapped by methanol to yield **methyl cyclopentanecarboxylate**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Intramolecular McMurry coupling of heptanedial ($\text{OHC}-(\text{CH}_2)_5-\text{CHO}$) using $\text{TiCl}_3/\text{Zn-Cu}$ in refluxing $\text{DME}$ gives as the major product
questions.explanationEn: Low-valent titanium generated from $\text{TiCl}_3$ and $\text{Zn-Cu}$ mediates reductive deoxygenative coupling (**McMurry reaction**) of the two terminal aldehyde groups of heptanedial ($\text{C}_7$ dialdehyde) to form a 7-membered cycloalkene, **cycloheptene**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of cyclohex-2-en-1-ol with $\text{CH}_2\text{I}_2$ and $\text{Zn-Cu}$ couple yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: In the **Simmons–Smith cyclopropanation** of allylic alcohols, the zinc carbenoid ($\text{ICH}_2\text{ZnI}$) coordinates to the oxygen atom of the hydroxyl group, directing methylene delivery exclusively to the **same face (*syn*)** as the $-\text{OH}$ group. Thus, cyclohex-2-en-1-ol affords ***cis*-bicyclo$[4.1.0]$heptan-2-ol** diastereoselectively. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Heating *cis*-3,4-dimethylcyclobut-1-ene at $200\,^\circ\text{C}$ yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: Thermal electrocyclic ring opening of cyclobutene is a $4\pi$-electron process, which is strictly **conrotatory** by the Woodward–Hoffmann rules. Rotating both C3 and C4 in the same direction (both clockwise or both counterclockwise) moves one *cis*-methyl group outward ($E$) and the other inward ($Z$), stereospecifically giving **$(2E,4Z)$-hexa-2,4-diene**. Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Heating *meso*-3,4-dimethylhexa-1,5-diene at $250\,^\circ\text{C}$ undergoes a Cope rearrangement via a chair-like transition state to give predominantly
questions.explanationEn: In the favored **chair-like transition state** of the $[3,3]$-sigmatropic Cope rearrangement of *meso*-3,4-dimethylhexa-1,5-diene, one methyl group must occupy an **equatorial** position (becoming $(E)$) while the other occupies an **axial** position (becoming $(Z)$). Therefore, the product is stereospecifically **$(2E,6Z)$-octa-2,6-diene** ($>99\%$). (By contrast, the *racemic* diastereomer places both methyls equatorial to give $(2E,6E)$-octa-2,6-diene.) Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding reactive intermediates is/are correct?
optionsEn: Triplet methylene ($:\text{CH}_2$) has two unpaired electrons and reacts non-stereospecifically with alkenes.
The cyclopropenyl cation ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^+$) is stabilized by $2\,\pi$-electron aromaticity.
Bridgehead carbanions such as the 1-norbornyl anion cannot exist because they violate Bredt's rule.
Benzyne possesses a weak in-plane $\pi$-bond formed by sideways overlap of two adjacent $sp^2$ hybrid orbitals.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Triplet carbenes are diradicals that add stepwise to alkenes, allowing $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond rotation before ring closure (non-stereospecific).
- **(B) Correct:** $\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^+$ is planar, cyclic, conjugated, and has $2\,\pi$ electrons ($4n+2$ with $n=0$) $\implies$ aromatic.
- **(C) Incorrect:** Unlike bridgehead carbocations (which need planar $sp^2$ geometry), bridgehead carbanions retain pyramidal $sp^3$ geometry and do NOT violate Bredt's rule.
- **(D) Correct:** The extra bond in benzyne arises from poor sideways overlap of two coplanar $sp^2$ orbitals perpendicular to the aromatic $\pi$-system.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (D)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about $\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ reductions is/are correct?
optionsEn: $\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ reduces carboxylic acids faster than esters.
$\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ reduces tertiary amides to tertiary amines.
Hydroboration of terminal alkenes with $\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ followed by alkaline $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ gives anti-Markovnikov primary alcohols.
$\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ is a nucleophilic hydride donor that reacts preferentially with electron-poor double bonds.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Electrophilic $\text{BH}_3$ reacts rapidly with $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ via a triacyloxyborane intermediate, reducing carboxylic acids selectively in the presence of esters.
- **(B) Correct:** $\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ cleanly reduces electron-rich amide carbonyls to amines.
- **(C) Correct:** Hydroboration–oxidation gives anti-Markovnikov *syn*-hydration.
- **(D) Incorrect:** $\text{BH}_3$ is an **electrophilic** (Lewis acidic) reducing agent, not a nucleophilic hydride donor.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the **benzilic acid rearrangement** is/are true?
optionsEn: It converts 1,2-diketones lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens (such as benzil) into $\alpha$-hydroxy carboxylic acids upon treatment with strong base followed by acidification.
The migrating aryl group shifts to an adjacent carbonyl carbon in the rate-determining step.
When applied to cyclic 1,2-diketones such as phenanthrene-9,10-dione, it causes ring contraction.
It requires a Lewis acid such as anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to initiate migration.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Benzil + $\text{OH}^-$ followed by $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ yields benzilic acid.
- **(B) Correct:** Reversible $\text{OH}^-$ addition is followed by rate-determining 1,2-aryl migration.
- **(C) Correct:** Six-membered cyclic 1,2-diketones contract to 5-membered $\alpha$-hydroxy carboxylic acids.
- **(D) Incorrect:** It is strictly base-promoted ($\text{OH}^-$ or $\text{RO}^-$), not $\text{AlCl}_3$-catalyzed.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements regarding E2 and E1cb eliminations is/are correct?
optionsEn: E2 elimination exhibits a primary kinetic isotope effect ($k_\text{H}/k_\text{D} > 1$) when the $\beta$-hydrogen is replaced by deuterium.
Quaternary ammonium hydroxides ($\text{RCH}_2\text{CH(NMe}_3^+\text{)CH}_3\,\text{OH}^-$) upon heating predominantly give the less substituted Hofmann alkene.
In a reversible E1cb mechanism, deuterium exchange at the $\beta$-carbon can occur faster than elimination when run in $\text{D}_2\text{O}$.
E2 elimination requires the leaving group and $\beta$-hydrogen to be strictly *syn*-coplanar in acyclic substrates.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** The $\text{C}_\beta-\text{H}$ bond breaks in the rate-determining step of E2, giving a primary KIE ($k_\text{H}/k_\text{D} \approx 3\text{--}7$).
- **(B) Correct:** Hofmann elimination of bulky $-\text{NMe}_3^+$ leaving groups favors abstraction of the less hindered, more acidic primary $\beta$-H.
- **(C) Correct:** In reversible E1cb, rapid reversible carbanion formation allows $\text{H/D}$ exchange with $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ before slow leaving-group expulsion.
- **(D) Incorrect:** Acyclic E2 eliminations strongly prefer **anti-periplanar** ($180^\circ$) geometry.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
Reaction of benzaldehyde with methylenetriphenylphosphorane ($\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$) yields an alkene as the major organic product. The molecular weight of this alkene is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$]
questions.explanationEn: Wittig olefination of benzaldehyde ($\text{PhCHO}$) with $\text{Ph}_3\text{P}=\text{CH}_2$ yields styrene ($\text{PhCH}=\text{CH}_2$, $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8$). Molecular weight $= 8(12) + 8(1) = 104\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of $\alpha$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds participating in hyperconjugation with the vacant $2p$ orbital in the *tert*-butyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The *tert*-butyl carbocation has three methyl groups attached to the positively charged $sp^2$ carbon, providing $3 \times 3 = \mathbf{9}$ $\alpha$-$\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds for hyperconjugation.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of $sp^3$-hybridized stereogenic carbon centers present in the *endo* Diels–Alder adduct of cyclopentadiene and maleic anhydride (3a,4,7,7a-tetrahydro-4,7-methanoisobenzofuran-1,3-dione) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In the *endo* adduct of cyclopentadiene and maleic anhydride, the two bridgehead carbons (C4 and C7) and the two ring-junction carbons bearing the anhydride carbonyls (C3a and C7a) are all $sp^3$ stereogenic centers (note that the molecule is *meso* due to a symmetry plane bisecting the C5=C6 and C8 bridges). Thus, there are **$4$** stereogenic carbon centers.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl}$) of acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) yields a hydrocarbon whose molecular weight is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$]
questions.explanationEn: Clemmensen reduction converts the carbonyl group of acetophenone ($\text{PhCOCH}_3$) into a methylene group, affording ethylbenzene ($\text{PhCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{10}$). Molecular weight $= 8(12) + 10(1) = 106\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Assuming all four $\text{Al}-\text{H}$ hydrides of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ are utilized, the minimum number of moles of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ required to reduce $4.0\text{ moles}$ of acetone to propan-2-ol (followed by aqueous workup) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Each ketone reduction requires $1$ hydride equivalent ($\text{H}^-$). Since $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ delivers $4\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}^-$, reducing $4.0\text{ mol}$ of acetone requires theoretically **$1$** mole of $\text{LiAlH}_4$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry II: Reaction Mechanisms, Name Reactions & Pericyclic Chemistry (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the free-radical monochlorination of 2-methylpropane (isobutane) at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$, the relative reactivity of a tertiary $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond to a primary $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond is $5.0 : 1.0$. The predicted percentage of 2-chloro-2-methylpropane in the monochlorinated product mixture is _______ $\%$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
2-Methylpropane has $9$ primary hydrogens (reactivity $1.0$ each) and $1$ tertiary hydrogen (reactivity $5.0$).
- Statistical weight of 2-chloro-2-methylpropane $= 1 \times 5.0 = 5.0$.
- Statistical weight of 1-chloro-2-methylpropane $= 9 \times 1.0 = 9.0$.
- Percentage of 2-chloro-2-methylpropane $= \frac{5.0}{5.0 + 9.0} \times 100\% = \frac{500}{14}\% = \mathbf{35.71}\%$.
